App details

Dialer

An Android phone app for calls, contacts and call history, with configurable automatic redial.

In the worksPlannedAndroid

What it’s for

A complete default phone app for Android, covering everyday incoming, outgoing and ongoing calls. Find people through the dialpad or system contacts, use favorites and call history, choose a SIM and keep call notes. Automatic redial has separate settings for intervals and attempt limits.

Main features

  • Dialpad, T9 contact search and favorites.
  • Incoming and ongoing call controls.
  • Choose a SIM, block numbers and add call notes.
  • Set redial intervals and attempt limits.

This app is being planned and is not yet available to download. The description presents its intended functions.

Features in detail

Calling, contacts, redial and your controls

Your default Android phone app

Set Dialer as the default phone app using Android’s system prompt and grant relevant access when needed. It provides dialing, incoming and ongoing-call screens using the system’s calling services. Losing the role or permission disables affected features with a recovery explanation. Android’s trusted emergency route stays in charge; app automation must not interfere.

Dialpad, T9 and speed dial

Enter or paste numbers, +, * or #; hold 0 for + and backspace to clear. Live number/name/T9 search includes accents. Hold 1 for the selected account’s voicemail and 2–9 for assigned concrete numbers. Empty-field Call first loads the last callable number, then calls on the next press. Add a number to Android contacts; tones, vibration and call confirmation are adjustable.

Contacts and favorites

Use existing Android contacts with phone numbers, current photos and starred favorites. Search, fast-scroll, sort names and filter contact sources. Choose a concrete number for multi-number contacts; grid/list favorites can be reordered by dragging. Call, redial, hand off SMS, copy, block or open contact details; home-screen shortcuts stay tied to a number. System contact editing keeps one contact book.

Call history, groups, tags and JSON files

View number/name, direction, date, duration and SIM in system call history. Search or filter all/missed/incoming/outgoing, expand grouped consecutive calls and use contextual actions. Select/delete records with confirmation. Label unsaved numbers locally without creating a contact. Free JSON export/import previews errors and duplicates; files contain sensitive call details. Blocked attempts have their own list.

Incoming calls and conversation controls

See caller and SIM, then answer or reject using supported buttons/swipe styles, including lock-screen handling permitted by Android. During a call, mute, use the tone keypad, change available audio routes, hold/resume, take a note or hang up. Waiting calls can be answered/rejected/swapped; conference controls appear only when supported. Leaving the screen does not hang up; return from the call notification.

Optional local call announcement

Choose Off, Always, wired headset, Bluetooth or either headset route for the free announcer. Select caller name and suitable number/type; a reliable unknown-number region can be read. Local/system speech respects sound/Do Not Disturb and never prevents Answer/Reject.

Local call notes and reminders

Take a text note during a call while Hang up remains reachable. Drafts save locally and stay separate for concurrent calls; edit/delete the saved note afterward in call details. Free stores up to 10 notes without deleting old ones at the limit. Premium allows unlimited notes and note reminders. No conversation audio is recorded or transcribed.

Numbers, contacts and safe pattern blocking

Block a concrete number or entire contact, including numbers later added to it. Configure unknown/unsaved, hidden or unidentified callers and prefix/pattern rules. Broad patterns protect saved contacts unless explicitly blocked. Temporarily disable the app’s enhanced rules without deleting them. Grouped blocked attempts stay in a separate history with unblock/copy actions; free import/export previews rule errors and duplicates.

Configurable automatic redial

Choose the target from a number, contacts, history or favorites, fixed SIM and attempt limit, then press Start. Set retry delay 0–300 seconds: zero adds no artificial wait; positive values are minimum waits. Busy can retry; for a call that never connects choose Retry or Stop. Proven local/SIM/network failure or unknown outcome stops. Successful connection stops automation while keeping the conversation; later hang-up does not restart it.

Stop, limits, preferences and session results

Stop cancels current/waiting retries so no delayed call can restart them. Free allows 20 attempts per session; Premium allows a chosen 1–9999. Optional time limit stops at whichever limit arrives first. See target, SIM, attempt/limit, wait and result; local redial summaries are separate from call history. Settings persist, but app restart never resumes a live session or calls automatically.

Dual SIM and per-number preferences

Use system calling-account preference, always ask or choose an available SIM. Remember a SIM for a concrete number; per-number choice precedes the app-wide override and system default. Holding Call opens the account picker without changing the saved default. An unavailable chosen SIM is reported rather than silently replaced; redial uses one fixed account throughout.

Layout choices, free phone features and Premium

Both Free and Premium are ad-free. Normal calls, T9, contacts/favorites, history, blocking, dual SIM and speed dial are free. Choose System/Light/Dark, start page, grid/list and basic size settings. One-time Premium adds larger redial limits, unlimited notes/reminders and deeper dialpad, tabs, call-screen/answer and list/grid layouts. Safety controls remain reachable; current local price and restoration come through Play.

Call behavior and display settings

Choose date/time and name/number formats, whether tapping a contact calls or opens details, whether the dialpad opens at launch and whether consecutive calls are grouped. Optional call confirmation applies once before redial Start. Advanced includes a proximity-sensor override; a shortcut opens Android calling-account settings. Incoming full-screen preference follows Android’s rules. Premium may show existing contact company/job-title fields on the call screen.

Local information and device migration

Country/region information comes offline from reliable number metadata, not a remote caller-ID lookup or the person’s actual GPS location. Phone information stays local without a JN86 account or cloud upload. Sensitive notes, blocking/redial history and SIM preferences may move device-to-device, excluded from cloud backup. System contacts/history stay in Android’s stores; app call-log and block-list file exchange is separate.

Use, settings and availability

Offline use

The main functions are designed to work on your device without a JN86 account. Purchases and external links may need internet.

Language, settings and help

Choose one of eight app languages and adjust the available settings. About provides privacy information and a link to voluntary JN86 support. Support does not unlock paid functions. Availability is shown below.

Availability

This app is being created. The features described here are planned; it is not yet available to download.
